lead: Aurora plumbing deals with cold snaps, expansive soils and homes from several building booms. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Aurora.
risk: frozen pipes and sprinkler lines, sewer lines cracked by shifting soil and basement water heaters
risk_short: frozen pipes, sewer lines and water heaters
why: Original Aurora and Hoffman Heights have homes from the 1950s and 1960s with galvanized supply lines and clay or cast-iron sewer laterals. Expansive clay in parts of the city moves foundations and cracks pipes.
Cold fronts freeze sprinkler systems, hose bibs and pipes near exterior walls. Many homes have basements with water heaters, sump pits and floor drains.
water: Aurora Water uses mountain snowmelt plus its Prairie Waters system, which filters South Platte River water through riverbank sand. Hardness is moderate.
tips: Blow out sprinkler lines before the first hard freeze.
Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
Test your sump pump each spring.
areas: PipeMend works in Original Aurora, Saddle Rock, Southlands, Tallyn's Reach, Hoffman Heights, Village East and every other Aurora neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Aurora Building Division, and plumbers must be licensed through the Colorado State Plumbing Board.

faq.a: It is Aurora Water's system that pulls South Platte River water through natural riverbank sand, then treats it. It adds a drought-resistant supply alongside mountain snowmelt.
